stories.headline: Epidemic prevention to be strengthened through coordination committees in Keralam
stories.title: Epidemic prevention to be strengthened through coordination committees in Keralam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Coordination committees, chaired by District Collectors, will be formed to strengthen local-level prevention of epidemic diseases such as dengue and chikungunya.
The Principal Secretary (Health) has been tasked to take necessary steps regarding this, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan announced after the epidemic review meeting here on Monday.
The meeting also directed that committees be formed at the grassroots in local bodies, by including councillors/panchayat members, residents’ association office-bearers, and health workers.
Dengue hotspots will be identified and mosquito control activities, among other measures, will be intensified.

To prevent water stagnation from intermittent rains and to eliminate mosquito breeding, Dry Day should be observed on Fridays in educational institutions, on Saturdays in workplaces, and on Sundays in households, wherein all potential breeding sources for mosquitoes should be eliminated.
An action plan will be prepared for this in consultation with the Local Self-Government Minister.
Directions were also issued to step up preventive activities according to the epidemic calendar, to strengthen fever clinics in fever-affected areas, and to start new ones where needed.
The Minister said that meetings of District Medical.
Officers and District Programme Managers will be convened to review day-to-day grassroots activities in the coming days.

Those who attended the review meeting included the Principal Secretary (Health), Sharmila Mary Joseph; the Chairman, Health Department High-Power Committee, S. S.Lal; the Director of Health Services, V. Meenakshy; the Director of Medical Education, K.V. Viswanathan; Head, Infectious Diseases Department, Thiruvananthapuram Government Medical College, Aravind R.; Special Officer, Kerala Centre for Disease Control, A. Althaf, among others.

stories.headline: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.title: Tirupattur TVK MLA’s win by a single vote: Madras High Court rejects election petition filed against his victory
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy to reject the election petition preferred by former DMK Minister K.R. Periakaruppan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) rejected an election petition filed against the victory of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA R. Seenivasa Sethupathy from Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district by a razor-thin margin of just one vote in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Asepolls.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by the TVK MLA to reject the election petition filed by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) candidate and former Minister K.R. Periakaruppan, who contended that he lost the polls primarily because of the existence of two Legislative Assembly constituencies with the same name ‘Tirupattur’ in Tamil Nadu.
Mr. Sethupathy was declared elected on securing 83,375 votes as against 83,374 votes garnered by Mr. Periakaruppan.

However, the DMK candidate claimed a postal vote belonging to the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district had been inadvertently sent to the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district and that the wrongly transferred vote was not sent back to the right constituency.

Listing out the reasons for seeking a rejection of the election petition, senior counsel V. Raghavachari, assisted by advocates Dixita Gohil and Pranjal Agarwal, argued the election petitioner had presented a “highly implausible” scenario of a postal vote belonging to one constituency having been sent to another constituency just because of their identical names.

He contended the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, make the identity of the intended constituency extremely difficult to lose by pressing into service multiple independent identifiers, which could enable the authorities to determine the constituency to which a postal ballot belongs.

The counsel pointed out the Tirupattur constituency in Tirupattur district was identified as constituency number 50, whereas the Tirupattur constituency in Sivaganga district was identified as constituency number 185.
He asserted that the constituency number, and not the name, was the key identifier.

He said every voter who intends to exercise his/her franchise through the postal ballot must make an application, using Form 12, to the Returning Officer concerned and therefore, the constituency gets determined emphatically even before the issuance of a postal ballot to an elector.

Further, the postal ballots have the full address of the Returning Officer of the relevant constituency pre-printed, without the need for the voters to fill it up by hand, and the postal covers too clearly mention the constituency name, number, district, and the full address of the Returning Officer.

“This means the postal ballot is not an anonymous page, which can ordinarily be treated as belonging to a constituency which happens to receive it by accident, coincidence, or otherwise,” Mr. Raghavachari said and added that it was the election officials who transport the postal covers.
The senior counsel also argued the election petitioner had not produced any material but for an affidavit filed by Tirupattur district DMK candidate.

stories.headline: India’s factory sector gathers steam, led by autos and capital goods
stories.title: India’s factory sector gathers steam, led by autos and capital goods
stories.summary: India’s industrial output grew 8 percent year-on-year in August, accelerating from 7.4 percent growth in July, according to data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI) on Monday. The jump in manufacturing and a rise in electricity and gas supply more than offset a contraction in mining in the same month.“This was aided by sharp growth in capital goods, intermediate, infra and consumer durable goods,” says Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, adding that if this growth momentum is maintained, India can register growth of 7-8 percent for the year on the back of higher growth during the festival season, with demand building up, which makes the third quarter “very critical” for industry.Chart: ﻿Manufacturing, which carries about 76 percent of the index’s weight, expanded 9 percent in August, compared to 8.2 percent growth in July. Sabnavis says that manufacturing did “very well” and that the auto industry contributed at both entry level and premium segments. In a note along the data release, the ministry highlighted that manufacturing has now clocked growth of 8 percent or more for three consecutive months, calling it a “record performance”.Within manufacturing, 18 of 23 industry groups recorded positive growth. Electrical equipment led with 30.9 percent growth, driven by switchgear, optical fibre connectors and UPS systems. Other transport equipment rose 25.3 percent, driven by two-wheelers and railway rolling stock, while motor vehicles grew 25.2 percent, powered by auto components, passenger cars and commercial vehicles.Also Read: Moody’s raises India FY27 growth forecast to 7 percentRubber and plastics (21.4 percent), computer and electronic products (19.3 percent) and fabricated metals (16.9 percent) also posted strong gains. Five groups contracted, including tobacco (-8 percent), wearing apparel (-7.4 percent), coke and refined petroleum (-0.6 percent) and chemicals (-0.5 percent). Sabnavis explains that the “industries which under-performed like chemicals with negative growth were affected by the energy prices issue due to the [West Asia] war.”Electricity and gas supply grew 12.3 percent in August compared to 8.7 percent growth in July, helped by a 15.4 percent rise in renewable generation. Generation from non-renewable sources grew 12.3 percent in the same month.Water supply, sewerage and waste management grew 6.3 percent compared with 7.4 percent growth in the previous month. Mining and quarrying was the lone drag, contracting 5.6 percent as output from fuel minerals fell 5.7 percent and non-metallic minerals dropped 12.8 percent.The use-based classification shows investment and industrial demand leading. Capital goods grew 16.9 percent, intermediate goods 13.7 percent and construction goods 12 percent. Together they were the top three contributors to growth. Strong growth in capital and intermediate goods points to sustained factory and infrastructure activity.Consumer durables rose 11.1 percent, while primary goods grew 3.5 percent. Consumer non-durables were the weakest at 2.1 percent.Despite the uneven spread, economists see the momentum as durable. “The revival in industrial growth is a positive sign as this has been witnessed in the last few months. Growth in credit to industry has also been very high and broad-based supporting the hypothesis of the sector recovering quite rapidly this year to contribute positively to overall growth,” Sabnavis says.

stories.headline: SC Collegium recommends 3 chief justices of HCs as judges of apex court
stories.title: SC Collegium recommends 3 chief justices of HCs as judges of apex court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the elevation of three High Court Chief Justices as judges of the apex court. According to the resolution issued by the Supreme Court, the Collegium recommended the elevation of Justice Sunita Agarwal, Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, as a judge of the apex court. The collegium also recommended the name of Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, as a judge of the apex court. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Chief Justice of the High Court for the State of Telangana, is also recommended for the judgeship at the Supreme Court. The recommendation was made at the Collegium meeting held on Monday. Besides the CJI, Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha were part of the Supreme Court Collegium. The Collegium's recommendation will now be processed in accordance with the established procedure for appointment of judges to the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court takes suo motu cognisance of recent sexual assault cases in Delhi-NCR, flags ‘lax patrolling’ by authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court takes suo motu cognisance of recent sexual assault cases in Delhi-NCR, flags ‘lax patrolling’ by authorities
stories.summary: The top court stresses that public spaces cannot be allowed to become ‘zones of high risk’ because of ‘lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies’
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of a spate of sexual assault incidents against minors and women in Delhi-NCR, seeking a response from the Delhi.

Police and observing that public spaces, including parks, buses and Metro stations, cannot be allowed to become “zones of high risk” because of “lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies”.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran took note of several recent cases of sexual violence reported in the national capital, including the alleged rape of a 17-year-old at Astha Kunj park near Lady Shri Ram College, the gang-rape of a minor at Swaroop Nagar, and the sexual assault of another minor inside a bus travelling from Greater Noida to Delhi.

“These incidents, considered alongside recent reports of sexual offences across Delhi-NCR, starkly underline the failure of law enforcement and public administration authorities to guarantee basic public safety.

The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution,” the Bench said.

The Bench further observed that public spaces, including roads, buses, Metro stations, footbridges and subways, cannot be permitted to become “zones of high risk” because of inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling and other preventable administrative deficiencies.

Expressing serious concern over the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year-old girl in a moving bus that travelled nearly 47 km from Greater Noida to Kashmere Gate in Delhi without being stopped at a single police picket earlier this month, the apex court said it could not help but “draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case”.
The incident, it said, called into question whether systemic law-enforcement mechanisms had made any “meaningful progress” in the decade since then.

While acknowledging that statements by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over such incidents were understandable, the Bench said expressions of solidarity, without accountability, failed to address the larger institutional question.
“Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil.

What is required is a measurable response with responsibility and accountability being fixed upon the authorities entrusted with prevention of crime, maintenance of public order and protection of vulnerable persons,” the Bench added.

The court also questioned the police response in the Astha Kunj case, taking note of reports that students of Lady Shri Ram College had previously complained of instances of sexual harassment in the area that had gone unaddressed.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks how children can have social media accounts, as underlying contracts are legally void
stories.title: Supreme Court asks how children can have social media accounts, as underlying contracts are legally void
stories.summary: Minors are legally incompetent to enter contracts under Indian law, notes SC; says social media firms must frame their platforms in conformity with Indian law, and enforce an age threshold of 18 years for ‘membership’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28, 2026) questioned how Indian children can have accounts on social media platforms, given that these accounts are activated on the basis of contracts drawn up between the children and the platforms despite the fact that minors are legally incompetent to enter contracts under Indian law.
Such contracts are completely void from the beginning or void ab initio, noted a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.
“What are these social media platforms doing?
Are they permitting children as young as 12 years to 15 years to have accounts?
Let us say Twitter: can a 15-year-old child have a Twitter account?
And what is an ‘account’?
It is a contract between the social media platform and a child,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, addressing the Union government side, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta.

The court was hearing a plea filed by Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA), an NGO founded by Bhuwan Ribu and represented by senior advocate H.S. Phoolka, seeking safeguards for children accessing social media and other digital platforms.
Justice Bagchi said a statutory framework has to be molded, using existing laws to specifically address these issues.
The Solicitor General submitted that the issue raised in the petition was, prima facie, covered by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
Mr. Phoolka submitted that the relevant provisions of the Act would come into force only in 2027 and therefore could not address the issue in the interim.

Acknowledging the submission made by Mr. Phoolka, the law officer said that “a similar regime can be adopted in other laws which say that if you are less than 18 years old, you will need parental consent, and the contract will be signed by the parent”.

stories.headline: Suo Motu Case On Delhi Rapes | Supreme Court Issues Directions To Make Public Spaces Safer; Orders Safety Audit Within 4 Weeks
stories.title: Suo Motu Case On Delhi Rapes | Supreme Court Issues Directions To Make Public Spaces Safer; Orders Safety Audit Within 4 Weeks
stories.summary: The Court sought the data on Fast Track Courts from the Delhi High Court Registrar General
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (September 28) issued a set of immediate directions to the Delhi.
Police and civic authorities to secure public spaces in Delhi-NCR.
The directions include a survey of vulnerable areas, a district-wise vulnerability map, patrolling at all identified parks, and a lighting and CCTV audit.
All are to be completed within four weeks.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran issued the directions in a suo motu case registered after a series of reported sexual offences against minor girls and women in the region.

The bench said public spaces “cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies.” It added that “expressions of concern, devoid of accountability, fall short of answering the larger institutional question.”
The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, must constitute dedicated teams for each police district, headed by an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
They will inspect vulnerable pockets, including outskirts, isolated stretches, parks, transport hubs, markets and educational-institution zones.
The audit must rely on National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data, local intelligence, past and present complaints and previous incidents.
The teams must identify locations where poor lighting, lack of surveillance, insufficient patrolling, abandoned structures or poor access control may increase the risk of crime.

A district-wise vulnerability map must be prepared and shared across adjoining police stations, so that information on recurring crime patterns and habitual offenders “is not confined to individual police-station jurisdictions.”
Patrolling and security arrangements must be deployed at all identified public parks and vulnerable areas at all times, particularly in the evening and early morning hours.

All are to be completed within four weeks.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran issued the directions in a suo motu case registered after a series of reported sexual offences against minor girls and women in the region.

The bench said public spaces “cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies.” It added that “expressions of concern, devoid of accountability, fall short of answering the larger institutional question.” The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, must constitute dedicated teams for each police district, headed by an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
They will inspect vulnerable pockets, including outskirts, isolated stretches, parks, transport hubs, markets and educational-institution zones.
The audit must rely on National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data, local intelligence, past and present complaints and previous incidents.
The teams must identify locations where poor lighting, lack of surveillance, insufficient patrolling, abandoned structures or poor access control may increase the risk of crime.

A district-wise vulnerability map must be prepared and shared across adjoining police stations, so that information on recurring crime patterns and habitual offenders “is not confined to individual police-station jurisdictions.” Patrolling and security arrangements must be deployed at all identified public parks and vulnerable areas at all times, particularly in the evening and early morning hours.

stories.headline: Noel Tata moots merger of 2 group firms with Tata Sons to keep it private
stories.title: Noel Tata moots merger of 2 group firms with Tata Sons to keep it private
stories.summary: Merge plan aims to push Tata Sons outside RBI’s NBFC and CIC thresholds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has proposed the merger of two Tata group companies with Tata Sons Private Ltd (TSPL) in an effort to keep the holding company private and outside the ambit of the Reserve Bank of India’s regulations governing upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs).
The proposed restructuring involves the merger of Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Private Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE), both wholly owned subsidiaries of Tata Sons, into TSPL.
Noel Tata submitted the proposal to Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran on Monday evening.
A copy has also been forwarded to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for its records.
The move comes weeks after the RBI, on September 11, rejected Tata Sons’ request to be declassified as an unregistered Core Investment Company (CIC).
The decision effectively keeps alive the requirement for Tata Sons to list its shares, an issue that has exposed differences between the company’s board and its principal shareholder, Tata Trusts.

Under the proposal, the merger would reduce the proportion of TSPL’s income derived from financial assets and investments in group companies below the thresholds prescribed by the RBI for classification as an upper-layer NBFC and a CIC.
Tata Trusts argued that the restructuring would restore Tata Sons to its earlier model of functioning as both an operating and holding company.

Farokh Subedar, adviser to Tata Trusts, said the Trusts had identified TESS and TCE as the most suitable candidates for the merger because it was the “cleanest option”, although Tata Sons could consider other entities as well.
While securing the approval of Tata Sons and its board could prove challenging, Subedar said he believes it would be difficult for the RBI to reject the proposal.
To qualify for exclusion from the RBI’s regulatory framework, the businesses being merged must contribute a minimum level of revenue and assets.
“We are looking at wholly owned subsidiaries so that there is no impact on the shareholding structure of Tata Sons,” Subedar said.

stories.headline: 68 high-risk glacial lakes identified in J&K
stories.title: 68 high-risk glacial lakes identified in J&K
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sept 28: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has acknowledged the increasing risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) in the Union Territory, attributing the growing threat to rising temperatures, accelerated glacier melt and expansion of glacial lakes. The government made the disclosure in response to an Unstarred Question tabled by Tanvir Sadiq, MLA Zadibal, in the Legislative Assembly. It stated that districts including Kishtwar, Ganderbal, Kulgam and Anantnag have been identified as areas facing GLOF-related risks. According to the government, the University of Kashmir has identified 616 glacial lakes across 12 districts, covering an area of 28.62 square kilometres, and has delineated 68 Potentially Dangerous Glacial Lakes (PDGLs) based on criteria laid down by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). The government said a dedicated Core Committee was constituted through Government Order No. 71-JK(DMRRR) dated September 24, 2024, to undertake studies and formulate measures concerning high-risk glacial lakes. The committee subsequently categorised 24 high-priority lakes into Categories A, B and C based on 17 risk parameters. The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) has also mapped 546 glacial lakes covering 20.25 hectares, while the Central Water Commission, SDC and IITs have mapped and ranked several high-risk or highly susceptible lakes, including Gangabal, Kousar Nag, Harnag, Mundiksar, Hangu Lake, Boud Sar and Sheshnag. For real-time monitoring and early warning, the government said the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) has been nominated as the lead technical agency for designing and implementing an indigenous GIS-based GLOF Early Warning System. A Memorandum of Agreement with C-DAC is currently under process and is proposed to include water-level monitoring buoy systems with satellite communication, automatic weather stations, camera-based Glacial Lake Vision Units, and a web portal with a Spatial Decision Support System for real-time monitoring and dissemination of alerts. The government also said a UT-level GLOF Monitoring Committee was constituted under the chairmanship of the Principal Secretary, Home Department, in April 2024 to oversee glacial lake surveillance, satellite monitoring, field expeditions, risk assessment and mitigation. The committee has held five meetings so far. During these meetings, decisions were taken on scientific expeditions to high-risk lakes, standardisation of risk categorisation, preparation of GLOF-vulnerability inventories, development of district-level action plans, community awareness and integration of GLOF-related information into disaster management systems. The government said district-level teams have also been directed to undertake downstream Hazard, Vulnerability and Risk Assessments (HVRA) and prepare actionable GLOF risk-reduction plans. Coordination has additionally been initiated with ITBP and Armed Forces outposts located near high-risk lakes for operating manual early-warning networks to alert downstream areas in case of an emergency. On preparedness and evacuation, the government said District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs), SDRF and NDRF are mandated to conduct regular mock drills in vulnerable areas involving Aapda Mitra volunteers, line departments and local communities. The DDMAs have been tasked with preparing district-specific GLOF Action Plans, including downstream risk assessments, mitigation measures and response strategies. Authorities have also been directed to identify vulnerable villages, hamlets and critical infrastructure, besides mapping safe evacuation locations. The government further said vernacular awareness material provided by the NDMA and awareness campaigns led by the Rural Development Department are being used to sensitise Panchayati Raj Institutions and downstream communities about evacuation procedures and GLOF preparedness.
